name: Macr
description:
The complete macOS experience for your Linux desktop.

A macOS menu bar and dock for GNOME. The menu bar has the Apple-style logo menu, the focused app's name and menu, the app's own menus when it shares them, a Window menu and a macOS clock on a translucent bar. The dock has frosted glass, magnification, a Downloads stack, a Trash, autohide and the genie minimize. Launchpad shows every app on Super, and Spotlight searches apps, files and settings with Ctrl+Space. Quick settings become the macOS Control Center, with Focus, app icons your theme lacks get a macOS tile, volume and brightness show as a pill at the top right, Alt+Tab looks like the macOS app switcher, and notifications show at the top right with a macOS Notification Center on the clock. The overview becomes Mission Control, and hot corners open it, Launchpad, the desktop and more. Stage Manager keeps the app you use in the middle and your other apps on the left, one click away. Windows that do not round their own corners get rounded macOS corners, app windows get the red, yellow and green traffic lights on the left, and the lock screen shows a big time at the top with your picture and the password field below, as can the login screen. Windows tile to halves, quarters and the full screen when dragged to the screen edges or with Super+Ctrl and the arrow keys. Super+Shift+3, 4 and 5 take screenshots as on a Mac, with a floating thumbnail after each one. Super stands in for Command to quit, minimize and hide apps, App Exposé shows all of one app's windows, and full-screen apps get a Space of their own.
